title: O Sacred Head, Now Wounded
lyrics_original: With grief and shame weighed down,
How pale Thou art with anguish,
Which once was bright as morn!
What Thou, my Lord, hast suffered,
Lo, here I fall, my Savior!
Look on me with Thy favor,
Never outlive my love to Thee.
Great blessings Thou didst give me,
Thy lips have often fed me
With words of truth and love;
Thy Spirit oft hath led me
My Savior, be Thou near me
When death is at my door;
Then let Thy presence cheer me,

bible_verses.english: But he was wounded for our transgressions. He was bruised for our iniquities. The chastisement of our peace was on him; and with his stripes we are healed.
They braided a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand. They kneeled before him and mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, “It is finished.” He bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.

devotional.prayer_english: Lord Jesus, my heart turns to You with deep reverence as I contemplate Your sacrifice. It was my sin that placed that crown of thorns upon Your head, yet You bore it all out of boundless love for me. Thank You for enduring the shame and anguish so that I might know forgiveness and life. Help me to live each day in awe of Your grace. Amen.

devotional.reflection_english: Looking upon the wounded brow of Jesus reveals the immense weight of love He carried for us. In His crown of thorns and pale visage, we see both the tragedy of our sin and the beauty of His sacrifice. He willingly bore the grief, shame, and scorn that was rightfully ours, turning our transgression into His grace. As we sing, we are invited to bow our hearts in humble gratitude, resting in the deep wonder of His redeeming love.
